blocks.text: Imagine a world where every device has a unique address. How do we ensure that these addresses are efficiently allocated and routed across the globe?

blocks.markdown: In computer networks, IP addressing is crucial for identifying devices and routing data packets across the internet. This lesson will cover the fundamentals of IP addressing, including IPv4 and IPv6, subnetting, and the motivation behind IPv6 and Network Address Translation (NAT).

blocks.title: IP Address
blocks.text: An IP address is a unique identifier assigned to each device connected to a network. It allows devices to communicate with each other over the internet.

blocks.markdown:
### IPv4 Addressing
IPv4 addresses are 32-bit numbers typically represented in decimal as four octets separated by periods (e.g., 192.168.1.1). Each octet can range from 0 to 255.

blocks.title: CIDR Notation
blocks.text: CIDR (Classless Inter-Domain Routing) notation is a method for specifying IP addresses and their associated routing prefix. It is written as an IP address followed by a slash and a number, e.g., 192.168.1.0/24.

blocks.caption: Formula to calculate the number of addresses in a subnet, where \( n \) is the CIDR prefix length.

blocks.title: Calculate Subnet Mask from CIDR
blocks.prompt: Find the subnet mask for the CIDR notation 192.168.1.0/24.

steps.text: The CIDR notation /24 indicates the first 24 bits are for the network part.
Convert the network part to binary: 11111111.11111111.11111111.00000000.

blocks.markdown:
### Subnetting
Subnetting divides a network into smaller, manageable sub-networks. This helps in efficient IP address management and improves network performance.

blocks.title: Determine Usable Host Range
blocks.prompt: For the network 192.168.1.0/24, determine the usable host range.

steps.text: Subtract the network and broadcast addresses from the total range: 192.168.1.1 to 192.168.1.254.

blocks.answer: The usable host range is 192.168.1.1 to 192.168.1.254.

blocks.markdown:
### Motivation for IPv6
The primary motivation for IPv6 is the exhaustion of IPv4 addresses. IPv6 provides a vastly larger address space and supports more efficient routing.

blocks.title: Network Address Translation (NAT)
blocks.text: NAT allows multiple devices on a local network to share a single public IP address, conserving the number of public addresses used.

points: IP addresses uniquely identify devices on a network.
Subnetting divides networks into smaller sub-networks.
IPv6 addresses the limitations of IPv4.
